title: Every ergodic interval exchange transformation is minimal
source_title: Ergodic properties of infinite extension of symmetric interval exchange transformations

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled lemma, retained line for line

standard_prerequisites.name: Ergodicity with respect to Lebesgue measure
standard_prerequisites.statement: The transformation preserves Lebesgue measure and has no non-trivial invariant measurable set of positive measure.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis, and it is used through the full measure of the set of points of continuity.

standard_prerequisites.name: Minimality
standard_prerequisites.statement: A transformation is minimal when the orbit of every point is dense.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the conclusion, and the proof establishes the equivalent epsilon formulation.

standard_prerequisites.name: First return map to an interval
standard_prerequisites.statement: The induced transformation on an interval J is defined by the first return time of the points of J to J.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the object whose maximal return exponent h and discontinuity set the proof controls.

core_obligations: Establish the equivalent formulation: for every x, y and epsilon there is a positive m with the m-th backward iterate of y within 2 epsilon of x (source line 326).

Take the interval J from x to x plus epsilon and bound the maximum h of the return times of the induced transformation on J, then let C be the finite set of iterates of the discontinuities up to time h (source lines 326-331).

Choose delta below epsilon so that the interval from y to y plus delta avoids C, and take a point of continuity of the induced transformation in that interval, which exists because the set of such points has full measure (source line 332).
Use the return time of that point to bound the distance of the backward iterate of y from x by epsilon plus delta, and conclude the equivalent formulation (source lines 333-336).

proof_roadmap.step: Replace minimality by the epsilon formulation and set up the induced transformation on the interval J.
Control the return times and pick a point of continuity close to y.
Turn the return of that point into the required approximation of x by a backward iterate of y.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 321-323: an interval exchange transformation ergodic with respect to Lebesgue measure is minimal. The proof (source lines 325-337), which the author includes for completeness, does not use the definition of minimality directly: it proves the equivalent formulation by approximation, which forces the introduction of the first return map to a short interval, the maximum of the finitely many return times of that induced map, the finite set of iterates of the discontinuities up to that maximum, and a choice of a point of continuity of the induced map, which is available because the set of such points has full measure. The statement records only ergodicity and minimality.
